en.title: Marvel Tokon devs admit it will be ‘extremely challenging’ to regain player trust after troubled PC launch
en.description: Marvel Tokon producer tells VGC the team is working urgently to fix PC issues
en.fullContent:
Marvel Tokon producer tells VGC the team is working urgently to fix PC issues

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls developer Arc System Works has admitted that regaining player trust after the disappointing PC launch of the game will be “extremely challenging,” and has offered “sincere apologies” to fans who have been affected.

Speaking to VGC as part of a forthcoming interview, Takeshi Yamanaka, producer of Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls, said that while the team has been thrilled to see the reception on console, he and the team are well aware of the issues faced by PC players.

“It’s been two weeks since the release, and we’re very appreciative to see that there’s been quite a positive reception from the players in regards to the game’s content itself, where we see the core fighting game player audience,” he said.

“They’re playing matches every day, they’re in training mode, they’re coming up with new combos, and we see them posting those on social media.

“However, at the same time, unfortunately, in the PC version of the game, there have been in-game issues experienced by many players, which we really apologise to the player base for all of these problems.

en.title: The new Halloween video game has been banned in Australia – and not because of the violence
en.description: Academics and a former classification board director say Halloween: The Game’s ban due to ‘incentivised drug use’ highlights an incoherent set of s...
en.fullContent:
Academics and a former classification board director say Halloween: The Game’s ban due to ‘incentivised drug use’ highlights an incoherent set of standards

Halloween’s Michael Myers is one of film’s most feared boogeymen, responsible for some of the most brutal on-screen deaths in horror cinema. The US video game developer Illfonic looked to reproduce those terrors in its upcoming title Halloween: The Game, with gruesome killings a major focus of the gameplay: for instance, you can stomp another player’s head through a toilet seat, or fry their brain by throwing them through a television screen.

But Australians will not be able to play Halloween, because it has been refused classification by the Australian Classification Board, which means it is banned from sale within the country. And it’s not because of the violence or murders.

In the game, players can smoke marijuana to see the location of Michael Myers in order to avoid being killed – a use of drugs that the Classification Board has deemed a “gameplay advantage”. Under the Guidelines for the Classification of Computer Games 2023, video games are refused classification if they contain “illicit or proscribed drug use related to incentives or rewards”.

“Halloween: The Game contains illicit drug use that is linked to an incentive or reward, in that use of the drug provides a gameplay advantage to the player. It is on this basis that the game has been refused classification, as required under the Code and Guidelines,” the board wrote in a recent statement.

In the wake of the decision, Illfonic’s social media accounts have been flooded with comments from irate Australians. An FoI officer said the Classification Board had received more than 500 complaints in relation to Halloween: The Game.

en.title: 'GTA VI' Cyberleek update: Everything leaked Tuesday, this week
en.description: Alleged clips of Grand Theft Auto VI simply cannot stop leaking onto the internet.
en.fullContent:
Alleged clips of Grand Theft Auto VI simply cannot stop leaking onto the internet.

After a few clips came out over the weekend and into Monday, there are now a few more, courtesy of the now-notorious leaker known as Cyberleek. As Rockstar and Take-Two step up their efforts to find and stop Cyberleek, clips keep coming out at an even more rapid pace.

We're not going to embed or link directly to any of these clips, but they are easy to find on social media. As of Tuesday morning, three new clips have surfaced:

A clip of protagonist Jason riding a bicycle on a beach packed with civilian NPCs

A clip of Jason looking around a fictional video game retailer, complete with a bunch of fake video game boxes

That brings the total number of leaked clips to 13, at the time of publication. To be clear, their authenticity has not been totally verified, but Rockstar and parent company Take-Two's legal efforts to stop them from coming out is certainly telling in that regard. In subpoenas, Take-Two has referred to the Cyberleek videos as "stolen content" and "leaked gameplay videos," suggesting they could be authentic.

en.title: What to know about the big ‘Grand Theft Auto’ leaks
en.description: This is read by an automated voice. Please report any issues or inconsistencies here.
en.fullContent:
This is read by an automated voice. Please report any issues or inconsistencies here.

See more from the L.A. Times in Google Search.   Set us as preferred

In the video game world, it’s one of the biggest releases of 2026.

For years, fans have been eagerly awaiting the sixth installment to the “Grand Theft Auto” franchise.

But the much-anticipated release of the game has been disrupted by a flurry of leaked scenes — such as a plane flying over a metropolis and the interior of a strip club — that has flooded the internet in the last week without the consent of its publisher, Rockstar Games.

Rockstar has not confirmed the videos’ authenticity, but its parent company, Take-Two Interactive, is taking action. The New York-based company late last week issued subpoenas to Microsoft, Discord, X and Google to track down the alleged hackers.

en.title: [UPDATE] GTA 6 Leaker Releases Game Store, Nightclub and Beach Gameplay Videos, Defends Crypto Scheme
en.description: UPDATE: CyberLeek has dropped a third GTA 6 leak video today following on fast from this morning's early releases featuring a nightclub and a beach...
en.fullContent:
UPDATE: CyberLeek has dropped a third GTA 6 leak video today following on fast from this morning's early releases featuring a nightclub and a beach scene — marking a significant escalation in the amount of footage hitting the internet.

This latest release of leaked material also continues to push CyberLeek's supposed agenda behind the leaks: an apparent dislike of the fact that physical media is being abandoned. "People are confused," reads the latest message watermarked into the footage. "This is not about actual discs. It is about ownership. Resale rights still matter — even in a digital-only era."

Fittingly, this message is overlaid on gameplay that shows GTA 6 protagonist Jason exploring a video game store, complete with spoof consoles (that look a lot like PS5) and game cases (I wonder if they include the discs!) There's even a sign in the store advertising "ex-rental games and movies for sale." Titles on offer in the fictional shop include games such as Glory Souls 2, Desolate Rim, We Came Together.

The leaks certainly appear to be ramping up ahead of Netflix's official GTA 6 reveal (check out the global release times here).

UPDATE: Hot on the heels of the nightclub gameplay leak, CyberLeek has released a 13th video, this time showing off Jason cycling on a beach packed with NPCs.

This new video includes the same watermarked memecoin advertisement and crypto statement detailed in the original story, below.
